about: D-321: the dressed stone's block-face detail set (tools/blender/blockface.py builds it, tools/blender/blockface.mjs drives Blender and KTX). Each layer is a tileable 2.048 m square at 1 mm per texel whose surface is CARVED: a quarry-rough face lowered by the strokes of a tool (every stroke a swept tool profile, the surface the minimum of the uncut face and every cut: material removal), then partly rubbed; Blender (Cycles) bakes its tangent-space normals and ambient occlusion from the displaced mesh (a 1 mm grid with a wrapped margin, so the maps tile). Packed RGBA per texel: normal x, normal y (OpenGL, x along u, y along v), height (0.5 + h / hscale), AO. The strip layers hold 16 rows of 128 mm each: v = the distance from the block's arris (the joint), u along it: the margin strokes the mason cuts along an arris and the chips it takes in handling and setting. Tool, stroke and chip dimensions are tier C (Q-484, Q-930): the toothed chisel reached Persia with Ionian and Lydian masons (Nylander 1970, 'Ionians in Pasargadae', RECOLLECTION); the 4 mm tooth pitch and 8 x 3 cm facets of D-218; the photographs of the ruin used only for the tools' marks and their proportions (UD-20).

layers.note: toothed-chisel face, lightly rubbed: the walls' finish (teeth 4 mm apart cutting ~0.45 mm, facets tilted ~0.7°; C, Q-484)
toothed-chisel face, another mason's hand (wider chisel, larger working patches), rubbed (C)
toothed-chisel face, lightly rubbed (the fresher finish of the newest work) (C)
flat-chisel finish over the claw's (a few claw marks left where the flat chisel did not pass): treads, landings, the tops of walls and copings (C)
point-dressed (punched) face: the foot's large rough-dressed blocks and dressed bedrock (D-232, C)
arris strips of a newly dressed block in use: margin strokes along the arris and the few chips of handling and setting (0.75 per metre of arris, 7-40 mm) (C)
arris strips of the rough-dressed foot: a pitched, irregular arris and larger spalls (C)
